title: k8s node provisioning & lifecycle debug scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for the 2/17-2/24 node provisioning flakiness incident. Mostly commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses and next steps. NOT an incident report - this is raw breadcrumbs for later cleanup.

TL;DR symptoms:
- New nodes (scale-up) intermittently end up NotReady or never register with the cluster (kubelet not starting / crashloop).
- A subset show image-pull failures for system pods (pause, calico, kube-proxy) on first boot.
- Problem seems correlated with specific AZ and an older AMI batch.

Timeline / breadcrumbs:
- 2026-02-17 09:10: autoscaler triggered +3 nodes in prod-us-east-2a.
- 2026-02-17 09:14 noticed 2/3 pods stuck Pending on new node (ImagePullBackOff).
- 2026-02-17 09:20 node ip appeared in cloud provider but kubectl get nodes shows NotReady.
- 2026-02-18 11:05 pulled one node, ssh'd in, found kubelet logs showing crash on startup (segfault in 1.29.3 kubelet).
- 2026-02-19 15:30 rolled AMI -> new AMI build; one node booted fine.
- 2026-02-22 repeated failures after another scale-up; looks like AMI pipeline re-used older image for a subset of AZs.

Commands & outputs (kept raw-ish):

# node list and status
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide
NAME                            STATUS     ROLES    AGE     VERSION   INTERNAL-IP
ip-10-0-12-45.ec2.internal      NotReady   <none>   4m      v1.29.3   10.0.12.45
ip-10-0-13-101.ec2.internal     Ready      <none>   1h      v1.29.3   10.0.13.101

# describe NotReady node (excerpt)
$ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-12-45.ec2.internal
Conditions:
  Type             Status  LastHeartbeatTime                 LastTransitionTime                Reason              Message
  MemoryPressure   False   2026-02-17T09:17:20Z             2026-02-17T09:17:20Z             KubeletHasSufficientMemory   kubelet has sufficient memory available
  DiskPressure     False   2026-02-17T09:17:20Z             2026-02-17T09:17:20Z             KubeletHasNoDiskPressure     kubelet has no disk pressure
  PIDPressure      False   2026-02-17T09:17:20Z             2026-02-17T09:17:20Z             KubeletHasSufficientPID      kubelet has sufficient PID available
  Ready            False   2026-02-17T09:19:30Z             2026-02-17T09:19:30Z             KubeletNotReady              runtime network not ready
Non-terminated Pods: (3 in total)
  Namespace     Name                                    CPU Requests  CPU Limits  Age
  kube-system   calico-node-xxxxx                        0 (0%)        0 (0%)     4m

# kubelet logs (journalctl) on node
Feb 17 09:16:52 ip-10-0-12-45 kubelet[1234]: I0217 09:16:52.123456   1234 server.go:341] Version: v1.29.3
Feb 17 09:16:52 ip-10-0-12-45 kubelet[1234]: F0217 09:16:52.223456   1234 kubelet.go:234] runtime network not ready: failed to set up CNI: cni failed: "failed to create"
Feb 17 09:16:52 ip-10-0-12-45 kubelet[1234]: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

# docker/containerd image pull errors (kubelet/journal)
E0217 09:15:11.987654 1234 remote_runtime.go:123] PullImage "k8s.gcr.io/pause:3.7" failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull image: unexpected EOF

# helm/infra actions we tried
- helm rollback kube-proxy to previous working chart (no effect on node boot).
- Pushed new AMI with debug packages, tested in staging (staging ok).
- Recreated node pool in problematic AZ (force new instances) -> improved but not fully resolved.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) AMI drift: some builds in the AMI pipeline still contain old networking packages / kernel / containerd combos that crash kubelet (high).
2) CNI manifests/daemonset race: calico pods sometimes crash due to image pull race on first boot and then kubelet reports runtime network not ready (medium).
3) Cloud-init startup ordering: systemd services start before containerd is ready; kubelet hits containerd API and fails (medium).
4) Underlying EC2 host/network quirks in AZ (low but possible given AZ specificity).

Things I tried (and why):
- ssh into node, systemctl status containerd and kubelet: containerd was crashing in one instance (segfault in runc-related path) -> suggests runtime mismatch between containerd/runc/blkid.
- backed out kernel update in AMI to earlier known-good kernel -> node booted and joined cluster.
- added readinessProbe delay for calico DaemonSet (testing); avoided immediate CrashLoop but not root cause.
- added extra logging to AMI build (write /var/log/ami-debug.log) to capture package versions at boot.
- ran kubeadm version check and compared on known-good node vs bad node (binary versions same).

Repro steps to test locally (notes):
1) Launch instance using suspect AMI in us-east-2a with same instance profile + userdata.
2) Wait for cloud-init to finish; if kubelet fails, collect: journalctl -u kubelet -b, journalctl -u containerd -b, /var/log/cloud-init-output.log, /var/log/ami-debug.log.
3) Try systemctl restart containerd; if restart fixes kubelet, likely runtime issue.

Quick actionable next steps (owner: me / Priya):
- [ ] Stop using AMI batch x.y.z for autoscaling until pipeline validated (Priya to coordinate AMI pin in ASG).
- [ ] Add AMI validation step: smoke boot + kubelet health + system pod pull in CI for every AMI build. (tracked in GH #412)
- [ ] Add more robust containerd+systemd ordering in userdata (systemctl start containerd before kubelet; add retries).
- [ ] Run a canary scale-up in each AZ with new AMI and watch for image pull failures (Alex helping).

Notes for post-mortem (to flesh out later):
- Capture mapping of failed nodes -> AMI build id -> builder image -> packages changed.
- Confirm whether garbage collection settings / disk pressure interplay caused CNI failures.

Random commands I ran (for reproducibility):
- kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-45.ec2.internal
- kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-45.ec2.internal --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa ec2-user@10.0.12.45
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | tail -n 80
- sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | sed -n '1,300p'

Useful links / references:
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/nodes/ (node lifecycle)
- https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/xxxxx (similar image pull race bugs)

End / raw notes. Will clean up and make a formal incident write-up after confirming AMI pipeline fix.
